title: Pace Median
statement: A running club records finishing paces one at a time in paces. After each new pace arrives, the club board shows the median of all paces recorded so far: the middle value when the count is odd, or the average of the two middle values when it is even (which may end in .5). Return the list of medians shown after each arrival.

hints.content: Sorting all paces after each arrival works but repeats a lot of work.
The median only depends on the largest value of the lower half and the smallest value of the upper half.
Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap.
Insert into the lower heap if the new pace is <= its top, otherwise into the upper heap. Then rebalance so the lower heap has the same size or one more.
The median is the lower top for an odd count, or the average of both tops for an even count.

testCases.explanation: One pace is its own median.
Increasing arrivals alternate between whole and half values.

solutions.title: Sort the prefix after each arrival
solutions.intuition: The median is read straight from a sorted list.
solutions.approach: For each i, sort a copy of paces[0..i] and read the middle element or the average of the two middles.
solutions.pseudocode: for i: s = sorted(paces[0..i]); m = len/2; out.push(odd ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2)
commonMistakes: Using integer division for the even case and losing .5.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Re-sorting after every arrival is simple and clearly correct, but it costs O(n² log n). Inserting into a sorted array improves that to O(n²).

solutions.title: Two balanced heaps
solutions.intuition: The median sits between the lower half's maximum and the upper half's minimum, and heaps expose both in O(1).
solutions.approach: lower is a max-heap (a min-heap of negated values), upper a min-heap. Insert into lower when the pace is <= lower's top, else into upper. If lower has two more than upper, move its top to upper; if upper is larger, move its top to lower. Report the median from the tops.
solutions.pseudocode:
insert x: if lower empty or x <= max(lower): lower.push(x) else upper.push(x)
rebalance so |lower| == |upper| or |lower| == |upper| + 1
median = odd ? max(lower) : (max(lower) + min(upper)) / 2
commonMistakes: Forgetting to negate when moving values between the heaps.
Rebalancing only in one direction, which lets the upper heap grow larger than the lower one.
solutions.interviewExplanation: I keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap, with the lower half equal in size or one larger. Each arrival goes to the side its value belongs on, then at most one element moves across to rebalance. The median comes straight from the tops. That's O(log n) per arrival. JavaScript has no built-in heap, so I wrote a small min-heap and store negated values for the max-heap.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: 3 → lower {5,3,1} is too big, so move 5 to upper {5,15}. Median (3 + 5) / 2 = 4.
